title: Company-wide policies & processes (Access, Change, Data, Procurement, Vendors, Travel, Templates)
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview

This page consolidates Redwood Inference's company-wide policies and standard operating procedures for: access & permissions, change management, data management, procurement & expenses, vendor management, travel, and the canonical internal templates. This document is intended for all employees and managers and should be referenced during onboarding, audits, and operational planning.

Owners & scope
- Document owner: People Ops (owner: Maya Chen, people-ops@redwood.ai)
- Policy steward: Security & Compliance (contact: security@redwood.ai)
- Scope: applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and vendors with access to corporate resources or handling company data.

1) Access & permissions
Intro: Access is granted on a least-privilege basis and reviewed regularly. All access requests and approvals must be auditable.

Roles and responsibilities
- Requestor: opens an access request with business justification.
- Manager: verifies job necessity and approves initial access.
- Resource owner / service owner: provides final approval for privileged resources.
- Identity & Access Management (IAM) team: implements access, runs quarterly access reviews.

Permission model (high level)
| Role | Scope | Approval required | Review cadence |
|------|-------|------------------|----------------|
| Employee (base) | Standard corporate apps (Slack, Google Workspace) | Manager | Annual |
| Admin (service-level) | Service consoles and infra config | Manager + Service owner | Quarterly |
| Privileged (SRE/Infra) | Production systems, KMS/HSM access | Manager + SecOps + CTO | Monthly |

Access request procedure (1-4)
1. Submit request via Access Portal (Internal app /access-requests) including justification and duration.
2. Manager approves in portal within 72 hours.
3. Service owner approves for resource-specific permissions.
4. IAM implements change and logs request id. Temporary access >30 days requires re-approval.

Deprovisioning
- Offboarding checklist triggers immediate suspension of all access on termination.
- Contractors: access end-dates enforced; renewals require contract amendment and manager approval.

Emergency access
- Use emergency access flow (break-glass) documented in Security runbooks. All break-glass events require post-event review within 48 hours.

2) Change management
Principles: Changes to production services or security-relevant systems must be classified, scheduled, and approved according to impact.

Change classification
- Standard: low-risk, pre-approved changes (e.g., routine config updates, security patches with no infra changes).
- Minor: require manager approval and automated CI gating.
- Major: require RFC, rollout plan, SRE sign-off, and a scheduled maintenance window.
- Emergency: unplanned changes needed to mitigate active incidents; must follow emergency change workflow and retro-review.

Change workflow (summary)
1. Create RFC (Request for Change) in the Change Log (confluence/eng-platform/roadmap). Include impact, rollback plan, monitoring, and test plan.
2. Routing: auto-assign to owners; minor changes need manager + SRE approval; major changes need cross-team review and a runbook.
3. Scheduling: production changes must occur in defined change windows (Mon-Fri 02:00-05:00 PT unless pre-approved).
4. Post-change validation: health checks, synthetic traffic tests, and a sign-off from SRE within 2 hours of rollout.

Rollback & auditing
- All changes must include a tested rollback path.
- Change records stored in the centralized Change Log for at least 3 years.

3) Data management
Data classification
- PUBLIC: Intended for public consumption.
- INTERNAL: Company-internal, non-sensitive.
- CONFIDENTIAL: Business-sensitive (financials, customer PII).
- REGULATED: Data subject to legal/regulatory controls (e.g., PCI, HIPAA).

Storage & retention
- Default retention: logs 90 days primary, aggregated 3 years; backups: 90-day rolling snapshots + monthly archived snapshots retained 2 years.
- Regulated datasets: retention and deletion policies defined per contract; contact Legal to confirm.

Access to data
- Data Access Requests: use Data Access Request form (DARS) and include business use, dataset names, and data owner. Approvals: data owner + data steward + manager.
- Pseudonymization: for analytics access, PII must be pseudonymized unless explicitly authorized.

Incident & breach handling
- Follow Incident Response playbook (confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security).
- Data incidents affecting CONFIDENTIAL or REGULATED data: notify Legal and Privacy within 4 hours, begin assessment and containment.

Data transfers & third parties
- Cross-border transfers: require Privacy and Legal sign-off.
- Vendor data processing: Data Processing Agreement (DPA) mandatory before sharing CONFIDENTIAL or REGULATED data.

4) Procurement & expenses
Procurement thresholds & approvals
| Amount (USD) | Approval path | Documentation required |
|--------------:|----------------|------------------------|
| < $1,000 | Requestor's manager | Expense form / receipt |
| $1,000-$25,000 | Manager + Finance reviewer | Purchase justification + vendor quote |
| > $25,000 | Manager + Finance Director + Procurement lead | PO, vendor contract, legal review |

Purchase process (steps)
1. Create a Purchase Request (PR) in Procurement system with justification, cost center, and vendor details.
2. Finance reviews budget and approves or requests changes (48-72 hours typical).
3. For recurring SaaS > $5k/month, Procurement will perform vendor risk review (see vendor management).
4. Issue PO and track delivery/activation.

Expense reimbursements
- Submit expenses within 30 days via Expense system with itemized receipts.
- Per-diem and meal limits: Domestic travel meals reimbursed up to $75/day unless actuals and receipts justify higher pre-approved spend.
- Card usage: Corporate cards must be used for pre-approved travel and recurring vendor subscriptions.

5) Vendor management
Onboarding checklist
- Business need and scope documented.
- Security questionnaire completed (vendor-security-questionnaire).
- DPA and contract templates reviewed by Legal.
- SOC2 / ISO reports reviewed for vendors handling CONFIDENTIAL or REGULATED data.
- Procurement & Finance sign-off.

Ongoing vendor governance
- Quarterly review for strategic vendors; annual review for others.
- Performance & compliance KPIs documented in vendor file.
- Contract renewal process starts 90 days before expiration.

Offboarding vendors
- Confirm data deletion or return per contract.
- Revoke all credentials and network access.
- Final invoice reconciliation and closeout checklist.

6) Travel policy
Booking & approvals
- All business travel requires manager pre-approval in Travel Portal.
- Flights: economy for domestic; premium economy for international >8 hours or with manager pre-approval.
- Hotel: mid-range business hotels with secure network access.

Safety & compliance
- International travel: register trip with Security and follow country-specific guidance.
- High-risk countries require additional approval from Security and Legal.

Expense rules
- Itemized receipts required for all claims > $25.
- Alcohol allowed when part of business entertainment; must be within reason and documented as client entertainment.
- Personal travel combined with business: incremental costs only.

7) Internal templates & artifacts
Canonical templates (location: confluence/templates)
- Purchase Request template (purchase-request-template)
- Vendor Risk Assessment (vendor-risk-template)
- Data Access Request (data-access-request-template)
- Change RFC template (change-rfc-template)
- Travel approval & expense form (travel-expense-template)
- Offboarding checklist (offboarding-checklist-template)

How to use templates
- Always copy the template into your team space and complete metadata fields.
- Tag the document with the relevant labels (e.g., procurement, vendor, security).

Governance & review cadence
- People Ops maintains this consolidated policy and will coordinate an annual review with Security, Finance, Legal, and Eng leadership.
- Minor editorial updates are allowed with owner approval; substantive policy changes require the cross-functional review documented in the Change Log.

Appendix A - Quick contacts

Revision history
- 2025-06-01: Document created by Maya Chen (People Ops).
- 2025-11-12: Added vendor onboarding checklist and procurement thresholds (reviewers: Alex Kapoor).
- 2026-03-04: Annual review and update to change windows and access review cadence (reviewers: Ruth Delgado, Noah Park).

Notes
- This page is a reference; teams may have additional domain-specific procedures that must be followed (e.g., SRE runbooks, product-specific security controls).
- For questions or suggested updates, submit a request to people-ops@redwood.ai or file a PR in the policy change log.
